newsitem.title: USA: Bando cuts qtly payout, cites lower net.
newsitem.headline: Bando cuts qtly payout, cites lower net.

text.p: Bando McGlocklin Capital Corp said Friday it reduced its quarterly dividend from $0.24 to $0.18 per share.
The company attributed the reduction partially to anticipated lower operating income after formation of a bank holding company later this year.
The first dividend at the new rate will be paid May 15 to shareholders of record May 5.

In other action, Bando McGlocklin said its directors have set preliminary terms for the spin-off of InvestorsBancorp, which is expected to take place in July. Each Bando McGlocklin shareholder will receive about 0.24 of a share of InvestorsBancorp for each share of Bando McGlocklin. Prior to the record date in July, Bando McGlocklin shareholders also will receive an information statement on InvestorsBancorp required by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
Bando McGlocklin announced plans in April to spin off InvestorsBancorp in order to maintain Bando McGlocklin's favorable tax status as a real estate investment trust.
Current plans call for the bank holding company to be capitalized at $7 million instead of the $5 million previously announced, the company said in a statement.
"We are pleased with the progress we now are making in obtaining regulatory approval for InvestorsBancorp," said George Schonath, chairman and chief executive officer.
InvestorsBancorp is expected to be listed on the NASDAQ.
Bando McGlocklin earnings for the quarter ended March 31, the company's first quarter as a real estate investment trust, are expected to be announced on or before May 15.
